summary: Newly reviewed November 23 manuscript of Borri et al. (arXiv first posted November 20) adds agent-specific evidence on US listed firms' job postings, especially non-senior roles. Observational panel and event-study estimates are not realized employment or definitive causal effects. No duplicate source found. Evidence-only intake because current validator requires unsupported numeric confidence for claims and impact scores for events; no fabricated scores or global promotion.

sources.title: The Rise of Agents and the Human Labor Market
sources.publisher: Borri, Cheremukhin, Liu and Tsyvinski (arXiv preprint)
sources.notes: Manuscript dated November 23, 2026; preprint, not established peer-reviewed evidence.

evidence.support: Panel analysis of 34.8 million US job postings matched to 1,784 listed parent companies finds one standard deviation higher market-implied agentic exposure associated with 2.11% lower six-month posting growth and 3.20% lower nine-month growth. Exposure is a stock-return sensitivity to aggregate OpenRouter agentic token usage, not measured firm-level adoption. Postings are not hires or payroll.

Event-study estimates after Claude Code 2.0 release associate one standard deviation higher pre-release agentic exposure with 4.54% lower six-month non-senior posting growth; senior estimate is statistically insignificant. Identification depends on comparable counterfactual trends and does not establish actual job losses or generalize directly to Vietnam.
evidence.locator: Introduction; empirical results by job type
